title: Panthers agree to 1-year deal with veteran LB Bobby Okereke: Source
content:
The Carolina Panthers made a move Saturday to address their second starting linebacker spot, agreeing to a one-year deal with veteran Bobby Okereke, according to a league source who was not authorized to discuss the agreement publicly. Okereke, 30, brings a veteran presence to a competition that features Trevin Wallace and Claudin Cherelus, neither of whom has distinguished themselves during the preseason.

The Panthers made a significant investment during the offseason in former Jacksonville Jaguars linebacker Devin Lloyd, who went to his first Pro Bowl in 2025. Okereke was a third-round pick of the Indianapolis Colts in 2019 who has collected 805 tackles and 7.5 sacks over seven seasons. He spent his first four seasons with the Colts and had a career-high 151 tackles and six tackles for loss in 2022, his final season in Indianapolis.

He signed with the New York Giants as a free agent in 2023 and has averaged 128 tackles over the past three seasons (46 games). New York released him in March in a cost-cutting move.

The Okereke signing feels a lot like the addition of tight end Darren Waller earlier this month — a veteran who immediately adds juice at a position where the Panthers believed they needed more competition. Dave Canales gave Wallace and Cherelus the entire camp to claim the LB2 spot opposite Lloyd. But other than Wallace’s sack on Davis Mills on Friday night, it’s hard to point to any impact plays from either player over the course of training camp and four preseason games. Bringing in Okereke also signals that GM Dan Morgan — a former inside linebacker — wants to shore up any trouble spots as the Panthers defend their NFC South title.

Like Waller, the 6-2, 235-pound Okereke is a low-risk signing with the potential for a high reward. The former Stanford standout racked up 149 tackles, including 92 solo stops, in 2023 during his first season with the Giants. But Okereke seemed to lose a step over this final two years in New York, when his tackle totals were still impressive but his ability to impact games with big plays was less evident. Okereke has long arms (34.5 inches), which help him get his hands on a lot of passes. But if his burst doesn’t return, he won’t be getting to as many as he did in his prime.
